scope: bounded two-pass read-only SHA-256 byte fingerprint of declared installed 0.3.1 dependency closure
byteFingerprintComposition: SHA-256 of newline-separated, sorted canonical JSON arrays of [relative pathname, file byte length, file SHA-256]; no file content or private path emitted
windowsStatClarification: On observed Windows host os.lstat and os.fstat exposed inconsistent creation/change timestamps for same file; checker compares shared dev/ino/size/mtime between path and open handle and compares ctime within each method before/after, reporting changes as unqualified.
limitations: The installed dependency tree is under historically broad-write H: ancestor ACLs; matching fingerprints are not trusted upstream package provenance or a clean-machine attestation.

The scan covers each package root enumerated through declared dependency graph and accepted npm lock metadata; it does not prove Node dynamic imports, spawned commands, browser/PDF helper downloads, or undeclared package roots.
Path and handle metadata were sampled before/after but do not provide race-free, cryptographically anchored Windows file-handle or loaded-process identity.
Whole-tree SHA-256 is a change-detection observation only. It cannot assert that the first observed bytes were safe, authenticated, or immutable.
Only bounded installed dependency package files were hashed; no production manager config, state, token content, account secrets, or user client configuration was targeted for read or publication.
Real standard DEV token effective-access checks, protected code/state namespace and roll-back proof require later separate operational approval.
